title: Divergent mechanistic reliance on the phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase (PI4K)/oxysterol-binding protein (OSBP) axis during Zika virus versus dengue virus and West Nile virus replication organelle biogenesis.

analysis.scope_and_question: Members of the genus Orthoflavivirus exploit host lipid pathways, particularly the phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase (PI4K)-phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PI4P)-oxysterol-binding protein (OSBP) axis, yet they display marked mechanistic divergence.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Recognition of this mechanistic spectrum is essential for accurate interpretation of lipid-perturbation studies and for the rational design of broad-spectrum or virus-selective antiviral strategies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Their RO biogenesis relies more heavily on viral membrane proteins (NS4A/NS4B), host reticulon RTN3.1A, alternative lipid-shape remodeling (including phospholipase A2-generated lysophosphatidylcholine in WNV, sterol availability, and fatty-acid synthesis.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: These distinctions have direct implications for host-targeted antivirals.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: PI4K and OSBP inhibitors show preferential activity against ZIKV, whereas SOAT1/2 inhibition exhibits broader anti-orthoflaviviral potential, and other targets (FASN, NAAA, ALOX12) display virus-weighted efficacy.

analysis.summary_en: Members of the genus Orthoflavivirus exploit host lipid pathways, particularly the phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase (PI4K)-phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PI4P)-oxysterol-binding protein (OSBP) axis, yet they display marked mechanistic divergence. Recognition of this mechanistic spectrum is essential for accurate interpretation of lipid-perturbation studies and for the rational design of broad-spectrum or virus-selective antiviral strategies. Their RO biogenesis relies more heavily on viral membrane proteins (NS4A/NS4B), host reticulon RTN3.1A, alternative lipid-shape remodeling (including phospholipase A2-generated lysophosphatidylcholine in WNV, sterol availability, and fatty-acid synthesis. These distinctions have direct implications for host-targeted antivirals. PI4K and OSBP inhibitors show preferential activity against ZIKV, whereas SOAT1/2 inhibition exhibits broader anti-orthoflaviviral potential, and other targets (FASN, NAAA, ALOX12) display virus-weighted efficacy.

title: Dengue Vaccines: Bridging Innovation and Public Health

analysis.scope_and_question: Dengue is among the fastest-growing mosquito-borne viral infections worldwide and continues to pose a major public health challenge because no approved antiviral treatment is available. Dengue viruses 1–4 and dengue disease; other flaviviruses are near-neighbour exclusions. Biologically related animal, taxonomic, model, differential-diagnosis and comparative entities are supplementary-only unless material target-specific evidence is also present; only explicit lexical or unrelated hard exclusions are terminal.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Several vaccine candidates have progressed through clinical development; however, questions remain regarding their efficacy, long-term safety, and ability to provide consistent protection against all four dengue virus serotypes. Over the last five years, findings from phase II and phase III clinical trials, post-licensure safety monitoring, and real-world effectiveness studies have substantially advanced the understanding of vaccine performance and influenced both regulatory recommendations and future vaccine development strategies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Clinical studies have reported variable outcomes, with several vaccines offering moderate protection against symptomatic dengue while showing differences in efficacy among serotypes and lower effectiveness in individuals without prior dengue exposure. Despite these advances, important immunological issues remain unresolved, including the induction of balanced and durable immunity against all serotypes, identification of reliable correlates of protection, and clarification of how age and pre-existing dengue immunity affect vaccine responses.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Current research is focused on developing next-generation vaccines that provide stronger tetravalent immune responses, longer-lasting protection, and improved safety for seronegative individuals. In parallel, innovative clinical trial methodologies and detailed immunological analyses are being employed to better define the mechanisms underlying protective immunity.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Consequently, vaccination policies have evolved toward more targeted approaches, including pre-vaccination serological testing in selected settings, preferential use among seropositive populations, and integration of immunization programs with vector control and disease surveillance measures. This review summarizes recent clinical evidence, emerging immunological knowledge, and evolving public health policies to provide an updated assessment of dengue vaccines and to identify key research priorities for achieving safe, effective, and equitable dengue prevention through vaccination.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on dengue vaccines, examining their development, efficacy, and public health implications. Dengue, caused by four serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4), remains a significant global health challenge due to the lack of approved antiviral treatments. The review highlights the progress made in vaccine development through phase II and III trials, post-licensure monitoring, and real-world effectiveness studies. However, key unresolved issues include the induction of balanced immunity against all serotypes, identification of correlates of protection, and the impact of age and prior immunity on vaccine responses. The review also discusses the evolution of vaccination policies toward targeted strategies, such as pre-vaccination serological testing and integration with vector control. Research priorities include improving tetravalent immune responses, enhancing safety for seronegative individuals, and refining trial methodologies to better understand protective mechanisms.

title: Unveiling the antiviral mechanism of A4S7: a synthetic antimicrobial peptide targeting dengue and other mosquito-borne enveloped virus infections

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the antiviral mechanism of the synthetic antimicrobial peptide A4S7 against dengue virus (DENV) and other enveloped viruses, addressing the need for effective antiviral therapies in the absence of specific drugs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized Vero cells and human cell lines (U2OS, HMC3, and IMR-32) to evaluate the antiviral effects of A4S7 against DENV-2 and other enveloped viruses, including Zika virus (ZIKV) and Sindbis virus (SINV).
analysis.methods: A4S7 was tested for its ability to inhibit DENV-2 RNA and protein expression, reduce viral progeny production, and interfere with DENV-2 binding to cellular membrane receptors. Molecular docking and FOPPR analyses were employed to understand the interaction between A4S7 and the DENV-2 envelope protein.
analysis.main_results: A4S7 effectively inhibited DENV-2 RNA and protein expression and reduced viral progeny production without cytotoxicity in Vero cells. It also displayed antiviral activity in human cell lines and showed no inhibitory effects against non-enveloped viruses such as enterovirus 71 (EV71) and adenovirus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interpreted that A4S7 might exert antiviral effects during early stages of infection and that its α-helical structure is crucial for its antiviral activity. Combining A4S7 with late-stage inhibitors like ivermectin or favipiravir resulted in superior antiviral efficacy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that A4S7 has potential as a promising candidate for the treatment of dengue and other enveloped viral infections, highlighting its broad-spectrum antiviral activity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the absence of randomized controlled trials and the need for further validation in clinical settings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the in vitro nature of the experiments.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the antiviral mechanism of A4S7 against dengue virus and other enveloped viruses, demonstrating its effectiveness in inhibiting DENV-2 RNA and protein expression without cytotoxicity. The α-helical structure of A4S7 is crucial for its antiviral activity, and combining it with late-stage inhibitors enhances efficacy.

title: Early warning of serotype replacement, spatial risk redistribution, and shifting clinical phenotypes: Insights from the 2023-2025 dengue outbreak in Meta, Colombia.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue remains a major public health challenge in hyperendemic regions, where shifts in serotype circulation, spatial transmission patterns, and clinical presentation can significantly influence outbreak dynamics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective longitudinal observational study was conducted using routinely collected dengue surveillance data from the Department of Meta, Colombia, covering the period from January 2023 to September 2025. Confirmed dengue cases with viral isolation and serotype identification were included.
analysis.methods: Temporal trends, serotype replacement dynamics, municipal-level spatial redistribution patterns, and clinical characteristics were analyzed using laboratory-confirmed dengue cases. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors associated with dengue positivity overall and by serotype, while interannual variation was assessed to evaluate changes in transmission intensity and the spatial redistribution of dengue transmission risk.
analysis.main_results: Marked serotype replacement was observed during the study period. DENV-2 predominated during the 2023 peak, followed by a decline and a sustained increase in DENV-3 and DENV-4 by 2025, while DENV-1 disappeared from recent records. Spatial analysis showed declining diagnostic positivity in historically hyperendemic municipalities and significant interannual increases in intermediate municipalities, indicating an epidemiological rebound outside major urban centers. Classical dengue symptoms, including headache, myalgia, and rash, were inversely associated with virological confirmation, whereas nonspecific neurological manifestations, such as somnolence and irritability, emerged as independent predictors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The dengue outbreak in Meta (2023-2025) was characterized by dynamic serotype replacement, spatial redistribution of transmission risk, and changing clinical presentations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Strengthening decentralized laboratory networks and closing surveillance gaps in low-endemicity areas are strategic priorities to improve early detection and outbreak control in hyperendemic regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations to the study design.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the 2023-2025 dengue outbreak in Meta, Colombia, to understand serotype replacement, spatial risk redistribution, and shifting clinical phenotypes. It found marked serotype replacement, with DENV-2 initially predominant, followed by a decline and sustained increase in DENV-3 and DENV-4 by 2025, while DENV-1 disappeared. Spatial analysis revealed declining diagnostic positivity in historically hyperendemic municipalities and significant interannual increases in intermediate ones, indicating an epidemiological rebound outside major urban centers. Classical dengue symptoms were inversely associated with virological confirmation, whereas nonspecific neurological manifestations emerged as independent predictors. The study highlights the need to update clinical screening protocols and strengthen decentralized laboratory networks to improve early detection and outbreak control. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and potential limitations in data collection.

title: Computational Insights Into the Conformational Dynamics of the Dengue Virus Capsid Protein

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the molecular mechanisms controlling the conformational changes of the Dengue virus capsid protein, particularly the opening and closing of its hydrophobic pocket, which is critical for its function in the viral lifecycle.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed computational methods to investigate the conformational dynamics of the Dengue virus capsid protein, focusing on its structural rearrangements and interactions with lipids.
analysis.methods: The researchers used molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling techniques to analyze the structural transitions of the capsid protein and the role of lipid binding in modulating the hydrophobic pocket's accessibility.
analysis.main_results: The findings revealed that lipid binding influences the accessibility of the hydrophobic pocket through environmental cues, and the open conformation facilitates interactions with lipids, capsid dimer stabilization, and immature virus assembly.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their results as providing a deeper understanding of the capsid protein's conformational dynamics, highlighting its functional transitions and suggesting potential targets for antiviral strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These insights contribute to the development of antiviral strategies targeting the capsid protein's conformational changes, which could aid in preventing or treating Dengue virus infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to computational models, which may not fully capture biological complexity, but the evidence is strong due to the detailed analysis of structural transitions and their functional implications.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the conformational dynamics of the Dengue virus capsid protein, focusing on the hydrophobic pocket's role in the viral lifecycle. Using molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling methods, the researchers identified how lipid binding modulates the pocket's accessibility, influencing interactions with lipids, capsid dimer stabilization, and immature virus assembly. The findings offer a deeper understanding of the capsid protein's functional transitions and suggest potential targets for antiviral strategies. While the study relies on computational models, the evidence is robust and provides valuable insights into the structural mechanisms of the capsid protein. The results have implications for the development of therapies targeting Dengue virus, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm these findings in biological systems.

title: Assessment of the persistence and recovery of dengue virus RNA in urban wastewater: implications for Wastewater-Based Epidemiology.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue virus (DENV) poses a growing global public health threat due to increasingly frequent and severe outbreaks. Moreover, epidemiological surveillance systems have limitations in the timely detection of outbreaks, highlighting the need for complementary tools such as Wastewater-Based Epidemiology (WBE).
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study aimed to generate further information on the persistence and recovery of DENV RNA in urban wastewater to support its monitoring through WBE. Two experiments were conducted.
analysis.methods: A negative binomial mixed-effects regression model estimated temperature-specific decay coefficients of -0.67 (95 % confidence interval (CI): -0.74--0.59), -1.25 (95 % CI: -1.32--1.17), and -1.31 (95 % CI: -1.37--1.23) at 4, 25, and 35°C, respectively. The performance of four recovery methods was compared.
analysis.main_results: Ultrafiltration showed the highest recovery efficacy (61 ± 8 %), followed by direct analysis (42 ± 10 %) and polyethylene glycol precipitation (7 ± 4 %). Skimmed milk flocculation yielded results below the limit of detection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: DENV RNA persisted in urban wastewater for several days at environmentally relevant temperatures, and ultrafiltration achieved the highest recovery efficacy among the methods evaluated, supporting the application of WBE as a community surveillance tool for DENV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the use of Wastewater-Based Epidemiology (WBE) as a community surveillance tool for DENV, which can improve the timely detection of outbreaks and inform public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study provides moderate confidence in the persistence and recovery of DENV RNA in urban wastewater, but it does not address real-world variability in wastewater composition or long-term stability under field conditions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the persistence and recovery of dengue virus (DENV) RNA in urban wastewater, aiming to support its use in Wastewater-Based Epidemiology (WBE). Two experiments were conducted: one assessed RNA persistence at different temperatures, while the other compared recovery methods. Results showed that DENV RNA persisted for several days at environmentally relevant temperatures, with ultrafiltration demonstrating the highest recovery efficacy. The authors concluded that these findings support the application of WBE as a surveillance tool for DENV. However, the study's evidence is limited to controlled conditions and does not account for real-world variability in wastewater composition. The implications of the study suggest that WBE could enhance outbreak detection and inform public health strategies, but further research is needed to validate these findings in diverse settings.

title: Changes in Dengue Epidemiology in China Before, During, and After COVID-19 2015-2024: A Retrospective National Surveillance and Spatiotemporal Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue remains a major mosquito-borne disease in China. However, comprehensive nationwide evidence on their long-term epidemiological impact is limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a nationwide retrospective spatiotemporal study using reported dengue cases in China from 2015 to 2024. Epidemiological characteristics were compared across pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic phases.
analysis.methods: Morlet wavelet analysis was used to assess temporal periodicity. A SARIMA model fitted to pre-pandemic data generated counterfactual forecasts for 2020-2024. Spatial patterns were evaluated using provincial incidence mapping, Global Moran's I, and Local Indicators of Spatial Association.
analysis.main_results: A total of 87 182 dengue cases were reported, with major peaks in 2019 and 2024. Imported cases declined sharply during 2020-2022 and rebounded after 2023, whereas indigenous transmission became increasingly dominant. Annual periodicity weakened during the pandemic but re-emerged after 2023. Observed incidence during 2020-2022 was frequently below counterfactual expectations, while substantial positive deviations appeared from mid-2023 and intensified in 2024. Post-pandemic dengue risk re-emerged in South and Southwest China and expanded inland, with weaker provincial clustering.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: COVID-19 and related NPIs substantially reshaped dengue epidemiology in China, suppressing transmission during 2020-2022 but followed by a marked post-pandemic resurgence, increasing indigenous transmission, disrupted but re-emerging seasonality, and broader inland spread.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can cautiously inform surveillance strategies, risk assessment, and public health interventions for dengue in China, highlighting the need for adaptive measures to address changing transmission dynamics post-pandemic.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on reported dengue cases, which may be subject to underreporting or changes in surveillance practices. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on observational data and counterfactual modeling.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines changes in dengue epidemiology in China from 2015 to 2024, focusing on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and associated interventions. It reveals a sharp decline in imported cases and a rise in indigenous transmission during the pandemic, followed by a resurgence post-pandemic. The research highlights the disruption of annual periodicity and the expansion of dengue risk inland. These findings underscore the need for adaptive public health strategies to address evolving dengue dynamics. The study uses a spatiotemporal approach, including Morlet wavelet analysis and SARIMA modeling, to assess trends and deviations. While the evidence is moderate due to reliance on reported data, the results provide important insights into how pandemic-related measures have influenced dengue transmission patterns.

analysis.summary_en: Dengue continues to pose a major global threat, infecting nearly 390 million people annually. This study models relationship between Aedes vectors and dengue pathogens, highlighting v c as a key driver of within-vector infection dynamics and endemic persistence. Using a predator-prey framework, we show that endemic conditions emerge naturally from the biological interplay between vector's strategies and pethogen pressure. Our results reveal that under tropical and subtropical environmental pressures, the innate immune system of vectors cannot offset high v c during endemic outbreaks, highlighting a fundamental biological trade-off: vectors can evolve increased transmission potential but cannot enhance immune capacity. We prove global stability of such conditions and determine thresholds of v c for three types of functional responses ( v c q ∗ , q = 0 , 1 , 2 ). Recognizing the importance of studying vector biology and therein vector competence ( v c ), recent research focuses on mosquito parameters to inform transmission modeling and vector control strategies. This constraint defines the limits of their evolutionary response to pathogen-driven selection and drives instability in disease transmission dynamics.

title: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify novel antiviral compounds from plant-derived natural products to address the unmet need for specific antiviral therapies against mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells.
analysis.methods: Functional assays were used to evaluate the antiviral activity of extracts, which led to the isolation and structural characterization of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins.
analysis.main_results: Five extracts significantly reduced DENV-2 infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. The isolated compounds inhibited DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents, with cross-arboviral efficacy against ZIKV and CHIKV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform the development of new antiviral therapies for dengue and other arboviruses, potentially reducing the global health burden of these infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a non-randomized, in vitro approach, which may limit generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate due to the preliminary nature of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study identified spirostane saponins from Solanaceae plants as promising antiviral compounds against DENV-2, with cross-arboviral efficacy against ZIKV and CHIKV, addressing the unmet need for specific antiviral therapies against mosquito-borne arboviruses.

title: Optimising malaria and dengue case management through optimal diagnostic test allocation under budget constraints.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of distinguishing between malaria and dengue infections, which present similarly as undifferentiated fever, and to optimise diagnostic test allocation under budget constraints to improve case management.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A mathematical model was developed to simulate the transmission dynamics of malaria and dengue in Burkina Faso, focusing on the interaction between the two diseases and their respective vector populations (Anopheles and Aedes) over a 104-week surveillance period in Kadiogo Province.
analysis.methods: The study employed a 15-dimensional ordinary differential equation model, coupled with the Pontryagin Maximum Principle and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions, to characterise optimal diagnostic test allocation. A forward-backward sweep method was used to solve the boundary value problem, cross-validated against a sequential quadratic Hamiltonian scheme.
analysis.main_results: The model achieved a coefficient of determination of 0.72 on the log(Y+1) scale for dengue, with an invasion reproduction number (R 0 d) of 1.57. The optimal dynamic allocation of diagnostic tests reduced disease burden by 24.6% at the baseline budget and by over 32% at double the budget, outperforming standard malaria-first practices in all 200 parameter draws under ± 30% uncertainty.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the optimal allocation strategy significantly improves disease burden reduction by leveraging the temporal separation of malaria and dengue epidemics, which allows for more efficient use of diagnostic resources.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a framework for optimising diagnostic test allocation in regions with co-circulating malaria and dengue, potentially improving case management and resource efficiency in public health settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on a mathematical model calibrated to surveillance data, which may not fully capture real-world complexities. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the model's assumptions and the limited scope of parameter uncertainty considered.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of distinguishing between malaria and dengue infections, which present similarly as undifferentiated fever, and aims to optimise diagnostic test allocation under budget constraints. A 15-dimensional ordinary differential equation model was developed to simulate the transmission dynamics of both diseases, incorporating vector populations and a constrained diagnostic budget. The model was calibrated to 104 weeks of surveillance data from Kadiogo Province, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.72 for dengue. The optimal dynamic allocation of diagnostic tests reduced disease burden by 24.6% at the baseline budget and by over 32% at double the budget, outperforming standard malaria-first practices. The authors interpret that this improvement stems from the temporal separation of the two epidemics, allowing for more efficient resource use. The findings offer a framework for optimising diagnostic strategies in regions with co-circulating malaria and dengue, with moderate evidence strength due to model assumptions and limited parameter uncertainty analysis.

title: Dengue in an era of hyperendemicity: clinical triage, case management, and primary care preparedness in resource-constrained settings: a narrative review

analysis.scope_and_question: This narrative review examines dengue virus infection and its clinical management in resource-constrained settings, focusing on how frontline health services can triage and manage patients across disease phases to prevent rapid deterioration.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The authors conducted a narrative review of the literature, synthesizing evidence on dengue management pathways.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Diagnostic confirmation and severity prediction are distinct tasks; safe disposition requires repeated assessment of clinical and laboratory trends, and outpatient care must be an active pathway with structured reassessment and individualized fluid therapy. Vulnerable populations need modified thresholds for observation and escalation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Existing evidence is largely hospital-based from Asia and Latin America, leaving major gaps in primary care, Africa, rural settings, fragile systems, and humanitarian contexts.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Primary care readiness should be judged by reliable performance of essential functions—structured triage, monitoring, patient communication, stabilization, referral coordination, and surveillance-linked surge response—and by translating clinical guidance into a consistently delivered frontline pathway.

analysis.summary_en: The review focuses on dengue virus infection management in resource-constrained settings, outlining how frontline services can triage patients to prevent rapid deterioration. It is a narrative synthesis of existing literature. Key findings highlight that diagnostic confirmation and severity prediction are distinct, requiring repeated clinical assessment and individualized fluid therapy, with modified thresholds for vulnerable groups. Evidence gaps exist due to a predominance of hospital-based studies from Asia and Latin America, underscoring the need for primary care data from Africa, rural, fragile, and humanitarian contexts. title: Association of dengue severity with the serotype of infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines the association between the serotype of dengue virus infection and disease severity, focusing on symptomatic primary infections and their outcomes, including severe dengue, dengue hemorrhagic fever, dengue shock syndrome, and hospitalisation. The central question is whether specific dengue virus serotypes are linked to higher severity of disease.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a systematic search of the Global Health, Embase Classic + Embase, and Medline databases using Ovid, including studies published up to 20 January 2025. The eligibility criteria included studies with matched serotype and severity information. A meta-analysis was performed using generalised linear mixed models, stratifying by prior exposure-serotype combinations and geographic region (Asia versus Americas). Heterogeneity was assessed using τ2 and I2 metrics, and risk of bias was evaluated using an adapted tool for prevalence studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The meta-analysis found that DENV3 in Asia resulted in the highest proportion of dengue hemorrhagic fever/dengue shock syndrome (DHF/DSS) cases among symptomatic primary infections, with an average of 21·00% [95% CrI: 13·02 to 30·44%]. It also showed that DENV3 caused the highest proportion of hospitalised cases (22·00% [95% CrI: 0·88 to 75·31%]) among primary infections.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is contrasting evidence on the relationship between serotype and disease severity. The review highlights heterogeneity in findings and the need for further research to clarify the role of serotype in disease severity across different geographic regions and exposure statuses.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to understand the mechanisms by which specific serotypes contribute to disease severity and to explore the impact of geographic region and prior exposure on outcomes. Surveillance and diagnostic efforts should consider serotype-specific patterns in disease severity to improve public health responses.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigate the association between dengue virus serotype and disease severity, focusing on symptomatic primary infections. The study included 71 studies from a search of Global Health, Embase Classic + Embase, and Medline databases up to 20 January 2025. The analysis used generalised linear mixed models to estimate severe case proportions, stratifying by serotype and geographic region. The findings suggest that DENV3 in Asia is associated with the highest proportion of severe dengue cases, including dengue hemorrhagic fever/dengue shock syndrome and hospitalisation. However, the review notes contrasting evidence and heterogeneity in results, highlighting the need for further research to clarify serotype-specific impacts on disease severity.

title: The circSNX6 restricts dengue virus replication in association with PARP1 and ferroptosis

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue virus (DENV) infection poses a persistent global health challenge with no specific antiviral therapy. Although circular RNAs (circRNAs) regulate antiviral immunity, their roles in DENV infection remain largely unexplored.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, transcriptome sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from dengue patients across disease phases and severities identified 15 circRNAs consistently dysregulated across all clinical stages, enriched in ferroptosis, glutathione metabolism, and endocytosis pathways.
analysis.methods: The study used transcriptome sequencing of PBMCs from dengue patients across disease phases and severities to identify circRNAs. It also included cultured cells and mice models to assess the effects of circSNX6 on DENV2 replication and related pathways.
analysis.main_results: Among the 15 circRNAs, hsa_circ_0031607 (circSNX6) was the sole circRNA linked to all three pathways and was upregulated in both dengue patients and DENV2-infected human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). circSNX6 overexpression suppressed DENV2 replication, whereas its knockdown enhanced viral propagation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Mechanistically, circSNX6 localized to the cytoplasm and interacted with PARP1.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings identify circSNX6 as a host factor that restricts DENV2 replication, offering potential insights into new therapeutic strategies targeting the PARP1–ferroptosis axis for dengue management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level evidence, and the results are based on in vitro and in vivo models, which may not fully represent human disease complexity. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of detailed clinical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of circRNAs in dengue virus (DENV) infection, focusing on circSNX6. It identifies circSNX6 as a host factor that restricts DENV2 replication through interactions with PARP1 and modulation of the ferroptosis pathway. The research highlights potential therapeutic strategies targeting the PARP1–ferroptosis axis. However, the study is limited to abstract-level evidence and relies on in vitro and in vivo models, which may not fully capture human disease dynamics. The findings contribute to understanding the host-virus interaction in DENV infection and suggest new avenues for antiviral approaches.

title: The capsid proteins of orthoflavivirus are interchangeable for West Nile virus assembly.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether orthoflavivirus capsid proteins bind genomic RNA through specific interactions. A critical step in orthoflavivirus assembly is the encapsidation of genomic RNA by the capsid protein to form the nucleocapsid, but the molecular details of this process remain poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized West Nile virus (WNV) and dengue virus (DENV) as model systems to investigate heterologous genome RNA encapsidation. The research focused on DENV-2 and WNV, with the latter serving as a related entity.
analysis.methods: The study employed a chimeric virus strategy to demonstrate that the DENV-2 capsid protein can package WNV genomic RNA if two critical elements are preserved: cis-acting sequences essential for RNA synthesis and the cleavage site required for capsid maturation.
analysis.main_results: The DENV-2 capsid protein was shown to package WNV genomic RNA when cis-acting sequences and the cleavage site for capsid maturation were preserved. The study also revealed that orthoflavivirus capsid proteins package genomic RNAs in a non-sequence-specific manner.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings provide direct virological evidence that orthoflavivirus capsid proteins package genomic RNAs in a non-sequence-specific manner, mediated by structural interactions rather than sequence specificity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These insights advance our mechanistic understanding of orthoflavivirus genome packaging, which could inform future studies on viral assembly and potentially contribute to the development of antiviral strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, and the findings are supported by direct virological analysis using chimeric viruses. The evidence is considered moderate due to the limited scope of the abstract.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the molecular mechanism of orthoflavivirus genome packaging, focusing on dengue virus (DENV) and West Nile virus (WNV). The research aimed to determine whether capsid proteins bind genomic RNA through specific interactions. Using a chimeric virus strategy, the study demonstrated that the DENV-2 capsid protein can package WNV genomic RNA if cis-acting sequences and the cleavage site for capsid maturation are preserved. The results suggest that orthoflavivirus capsid proteins package genomic RNAs in a non-sequence-specific manner, mediated by structural interactions. These findings contribute to the understanding of viral assembly mechanisms and highlight the conserved packaging function of capsid proteins across orthoflaviviruses. The study is based on abstract-only evidence, and the findings are considered moderate in strength due to the limited scope of the data provided.

title: Interferon gamma and inflammatory response genes by weighted gene co-expression network analysis reveal significant associations with severe dengue infection in India

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to understand the immune response to dengue infection and identify potential clinical biomarkers for severe disease. India carries 34% of global cases, yet studies to understand how the immune system reacts to dengue infection remain limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study analyzed early transcriptional signatures from whole blood of 112 NS1 positive hospital-reported dengue patients and dissected biological processes linked to varying disease severities, with and without warning signs.
analysis.methods: Differential gene expression analysis was used to identify gene patterns associated with severe dengue infection, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was employed to link gene modules to clinical traits.
analysis.main_results: Differential gene expression analysis showed suppressed innate response in WS patients, with downregulated cytokines (CXCL8, CXCL16, CXCL2, IL1B) and disrupted platelet function. CTTN, involved in maintenance of vascular permeability, showed the highest significant association with low platelet count.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the role of interferon response and inflammation in severe dengue outcomes, identifying key genes such as IFI44L, IFI35, OAS1, HERC6, and SAMDL9. It also emphasizes the importance of CTTN in vascular permeability and platelet count.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may contribute to improving diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for severe dengue by identifying potential biomarkers and pathways involved in disease progression.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results are based on a single cohort of patients. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of detailed statistical analysis and external validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the immune response to dengue infection in India, focusing on the transcriptional signatures of 112 NS1 positive patients. Using differential gene expression and WGCNA, it identifies suppressed innate responses and disrupted platelet function in severe cases. Key genes like IFI44L and CTTN are highlighted for their potential roles in disease severity. The findings may inform improved diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for severe dengue. However, the study is based on abstract-only data, limiting the confidence in its conclusions to a moderate level.

title: Association of NS1 Antigen, IgM/IgG Antibodies with Haematological Indices and Inflammatory Markers in Suspected Dengue Cases: A Cross-sectional Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue Virus (DENV) has been re-emerging as a major public health challenge in tropical and subtropical regions, including India, with increasing incidence, changing epidemiology, and seasonal outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted from March 2025 to December 2025 at Adarsh Multispecialty Hospital, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India. The study included 154 patients presenting with Acute Febrile Illness (AFI).
analysis.methods: DENV diagnosis was performed using an immunochromatographic kit for NS1 antigen and IgM and IgG antibodies from the serum sample. Haematological indices, Inflammation markers and liver function tests Serum Glutamic Pyruvic Transaminase (SGPT) and Serum Glutamic Oxaloacetic Transaminase (SGOT) were examined. Chi-square test was used for statistical analysis, and a p-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
analysis.main_results: A total of 154 suspected Dengue Fever (DF) samples were collected, out of which 38 cases of dengue infection were confirmed. The highest positivity was seen in the age group of 21 to 30 years, 14 (36.8%), with males being more affected, making up 24 (63.2%) of the cases. Testing for the NS1 antigen alone found 17/74 (23%) of infections, but combining NS1 and antibody testing raised the rate to about 20/73 (27.3%). Dengue patients showed significantly decreased platelet counts 35/38 (92.1%), White Blood Cell (WBC) counts 21/38 (55.26%), and also lymphocyte counts 20/38 (52.63%). Liver enzymes were also elevated (SGOT 161.58±372.44 U/L and SGPT 187.46±456.09 U/L).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Detection of the NS1 antigen with antibody testing gives more specific results. Integrated haematological, and inflammatory markers facilitate efficient risk stratification and enhance early dengue identification, enabling prompt clinical therapy during periods of peak transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Significant increase in CRP levels and a drop in platelet levels in dengue-positive patients are early indicators of presumptive diagnosis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate the association of serological markers with haematological, biochemical, and inflammatory parameters in clinically suspected dengue cases. Conducted at Adarsh Multispecialty Hospital in Gujarat, India, from March to December 2025, the study included 154 patients with acute febrile illness. DENV diagnosis was performed using an immunochromatographic kit for NS1 antigen and IgM/IgG antibodies. The results showed that 38 out of 154 samples were confirmed as dengue infections, with the highest positivity in the 21-30 age group and among males. Dengue patients exhibited significantly decreased platelet and white blood cell counts, elevated liver enzymes, and increased CRP and ESR levels. The authors concluded that combining NS1 antigen and antibody testing improves diagnostic specificity, and integrated haematological and inflammatory markers can aid in early identification and risk stratification. The study provides insights into the clinical and laboratory features of dengue infection, which may inform early diagnosis and management strategies during peak transmission periods.

title: The Evolution of Dengue Virus in India

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the evolution of dengue virus (DENV) in India, specifically examining how transmission bottlenecks and immunological pressures influence its genetic changes. The central question is how these evolutionary dynamics contribute to the emergence of new genotypes and the severity of dengue disease.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis that explores the mechanisms driving DENV evolution, including viral transmission bottlenecks, intrahost genetic diversity, and host immune responses. It does not report on specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Dengue virus evolution in India is driven by transmission bottlenecks and immunological pressures, leading to mutations that cause antigenic changes and genotype replacement. These changes are directly correlated with epidemic magnitude and severe disease outcomes.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the periodic recurrence of outbreaks and cocirculation of all four serotypes present challenges in disease control. It highlights how these changes lead to antigenic shifts and genotype replacement, which are associated with increased epidemic severity. The review also discusses the challenges posed by the periodic outbreaks and the cocirculation of all four DENV serotypes. It underscores the importance of understanding DENV evolution for vaccine development and public health interventions, particularly given India's high dengue burden. The review notes that while the spatiotemporal dynamics of DENV serotypes are linked to transmission patterns, the exact mechanisms remain unclear, creating a need for further research.

title: Insecticide Esistance Status, Mechanism and Control Measures of Dengue Vector Aedes aegypti: A Systematic Review

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the insecticide resistance status, mechanisms, and control measures of Aedes aegypti, the primary vector of dengue virus. The central question is to evaluate the current resistance trends and their implications for vector control strategies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of existing literature on insecticide resistance in Aedes aegypti. It includes studies on resistance mechanisms and control measures, with an emphasis on biochemical processes and practical interventions.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that Aedes aegypti has developed significant resistance to pyrethroids, particularly permethrin and deltamethrin, while remaining relatively susceptible to organophosphates such as malathion and fenitrothion. Four main resistance mechanisms are identified: Altered target-site resistance, Metabolic resistance, Penetration resistance, and Behavioral resistance.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the need for further research to address knowledge gaps and develop effective alternatives to conventional insecticides. There is limited data on the effectiveness of newer control methods in different geographic regions and populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests exploring plant-based compounds, biological control agents, and the sterile insect technique as potential alternatives to conventional insecticides for controlling Aedes aegypti populations. These methods could help mitigate the growing problem of insecticide resistance.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines the insecticide resistance status, mechanisms, and control measures of Aedes aegypti, the primary vector of dengue virus. It highlights the increasing resistance to pyrethroids, particularly permethrin and deltamethrin, and identifies four main resistance mechanisms. The review emphasizes the need for further research and the exploration of alternative control strategies such as plant-based compounds, biological agents, and sterile insect techniques to address the growing challenge of insecticide resistance. The findings underscore the importance of developing new methods to effectively manage Aedes aegypti populations and reduce the transmission of dengue virus.

title: Assessment of the healthcare burden of dengue disease in England: a retrospective analysis (2010-2023).

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the healthcare burden of dengue in England from 2010 to 2023, addressing the increasing incidence of dengue cases following global trends.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective, descriptive, cohort study was conducted using data from National Health Service healthcare records, linked with Hospital Episode Statistics and Office for National Statistics mortality data, spanning from 2010 to 2023.
analysis.methods: Data were collected from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum, Hospital Episode Statistics, and Office for National Statistics mortality data, focusing on hospitalized dengue cases and suspected cases in primary care.
analysis.main_results: The incidence rate of hospitalized dengue increased progressively from 2010 to 2019, with the highest rate in 2019 (5.8 per million person-years). The rate increased again in 2022 after COVID-19 lockdowns. Approximately one-third of hospitalized dengue cases were aged 18-29 years, and the most common complication was gastrointestinal conditions. Healthcare costs were primarily driven by inpatient admission costs, with ~20% of cases having a subsequent hospital admission.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that the increasing incidence of dengue cases in England aligns with global trends, highlighting the need for targeted public health strategies, particularly among younger travellers. Improvements in general practitioners' reporting of suspected dengue cases and associated details of symptoms and travel history are warranted.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a growing healthcare burden of imported dengue in England, indicating the importance of public health strategies to manage and prevent the disease, especially among younger travellers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective nature and reliance on linked healthcare records, which may introduce biases. The sample size is adequate for trend analysis but may not be representative of the entire population. The study does not provide causal evidence and is descriptive in nature.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the healthcare burden of dengue in England from 2010 to 2023, finding an increasing incidence rate, particularly among younger travellers, and highlighting the need for targeted public health strategies.

title: Thiazolidine‐2,4‐dione and Thiazole Derivatives as Privileged Structures for Dengue Virus: A Review of Medicinal Chemistry Aspects

analysis.scope_and_question: Dengue fever is one of the greatest global health crises, with millions of infections annually and no effective antiviral therapy available. The search for new antiviral drugs is not only necessary, but urgent. Dengue viruses 1–4 and dengue disease; other flaviviruses are near-neighbour exclusions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The present study offers an in-depth and innovative analysis of the therapeutic potential of these molecules, exploring in vitro and in silico assays and pharmacokinetic improvement strategies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The results reveal that TZDs and thiazoles have high affinity for strategic viral targets, effectively interrupting the DENV replication cycle and reducing the immunopathological effects of the infection.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The high morbidity and mortality rate, combined with the rapid spread of the virus, highlights a critical failure in the fight against the disease.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Recently, thiazolidinedione (TZD) and thiazole derivatives have emerged as potential candidates for the treatment of dengue fever, challenging the paradigms of conventional therapies. Unlike conventional antivirals, which fail to target a single mechanism of action, these molecules offer a multifunctional and disruptive approach, potentially redefining the treatment of dengue.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on the therapeutic potential of thiazolidinedione (TZD) and thiazole derivatives against dengue virus. It highlights the urgent need for effective antiviral therapies due to the high morbidity and mortality rates associated with dengue fever. The study explores the in vitro and in silico properties of these compounds, emphasizing their ability to inhibit key viral enzymes such as NS2B-NS3 protease and NS5 RNA polymerase, as well as modulate the inflammatory response. The findings suggest that these molecules could offer a multifunctional approach to treating dengue, potentially redefining current therapeutic strategies. However, the review notes the lack of established antiviral therapies and the need for further preclinical and clinical investigations to validate these promising results.

title: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever Case Prediction Using Climate and Social Media Data with Support Vector Regression

analysis.research_question_and_background: The dataset covers 2010–2024 and combines annual DHF case records, annual and seasonal climate indices from Juanda and Tanjung Perak stations, and 320 Indonesian-language tweets related to DHF in Surabaya.
analysis.study_design_and_population: SVR achieved the best performance with an MAE of 386.31 cases, RMSE of 556.86 cases, and R2 of 0.0121, outperforming Ridge Regression with an MAE of 601.31, RMSE of 727.19, and R2 of −0.6846.
analysis.methods: This study aims to develop an informatics-based model for predicting annual DHF cases by integrating climate and Twitter/X data and comparing Support Vector Regression (SVR) with Ridge Regression.
analysis.main_results: Model performance was evaluated using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation for 2011–2024 based on MAE, RMSE, and R2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This study demonstrates the potential of multisource data integration for data-driven dengue early warning systems.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) remains a recurring public health problem in Surabaya, with transmission influenced by climatic variability and potentially reflected in social media activity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: These findings indicate that SVR better captures nonlinear relationships in multisource dengue data, although explanatory power remains limited by few annual observations and high feature dimensionality.

analysis.summary_en: The dataset covers 2010–2024 and combines annual DHF case records, annual and seasonal climate indices from Juanda and Tanjung Perak stations, and 320 Indonesian-language tweets related to DHF in Surabaya. SVR achieved the best performance with an MAE of 386.31 cases, RMSE of 556.86 cases, and R2 of 0.0121, outperforming Ridge Regression with an MAE of 601.31, RMSE of 727.19, and R2 of −0.6846. This study aims to develop an informatics-based model for predicting annual DHF cases by integrating climate and Twitter/X data and comparing Support Vector Regression (SVR) with Ridge Regression. Model performance was evaluated using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation for 2011–2024 based on MAE, RMSE, and R2. This study demonstrates the potential of multisource data integration for data-driven dengue early warning systems. Dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) remains a recurring public health problem in Surabaya, with transmission influenced by climatic variability and potentially reflected in social media activity. These findings indicate that SVR better captures nonlinear relationships in multisource dengue data, although explanatory power remains limited by few annual observations and high feature dimensionality.

title: Shared evidence, different recommendations: a comparative analysis of Qdenga (TAK-003) dengue vaccine guidance for travellers across countries.

analysis.scope_and_question: This study compared guidance on the use of Qdenga (TAK-003) dengue vaccine for travellers across countries, focusing on variations in recommendations based on dengue immune status and other factors.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a comparative analysis of national guidance on Qdenga use for travellers, using survey data and structured review of publicly available recommendations. Guidance was synthesized according to dengue immune status and mapped across recurring decision domains.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There was broad agreement in recommending vaccination for travellers with laboratory-confirmed prior dengue infection. However, recommendations for those without documented infection varied widely. All advisory bodies considered destination-specific dengue risk but differed in whether and how they used travel duration, repeated or cumulative exposure, traveller characteristics and host susceptibility factors to determine vaccine eligibility.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Variation in Qdenga guidance reflects differences in how advisory bodies interpret shared evidence and manage uncertainty arising from data gaps and differences between trial populations and travellers. Additional data on vaccine effectiveness and clinical outcomes among seronegative travellers and older adults may help reduce uncertainty and support greater alignment of future recommendations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Transparency and shared clinical decision-making remain essential when discussing dengue vaccination with travellers.

analysis.summary_en: This review article compares dengue vaccine guidance for travellers across countries, focusing on the Qdenga (TAK-003) vaccine. It highlights variations in recommendations based on dengue immune status and other factors, despite shared evidence. The study found broad agreement on vaccinating travellers with prior dengue infection but significant differences for those without documented infection. Advisory bodies considered destination-specific risk but varied in their use of travel duration, exposure, and host factors. The article emphasizes the need for transparency and shared decision-making, and suggests that additional data on vaccine effectiveness among seronegative travellers and older adults could reduce uncertainty and align future recommendations.

title: Dengue virus 2 lacking N153 glycosylation displayed enhanced recognition by neutralizing antibodies

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how the absence of N153 glycosylation in dengue virus 2 affects its recognition by neutralizing antibodies. This is important for understanding potential vaccine targets.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a mouse model to compare the infection dynamics of the N153Q dengue virus 2 mutant with the wild-type virus. The research was conducted in an abstract-only format, focusing on structural and functional analyses.
analysis.methods: The researchers compared cryoEM structures of wild-type and mutant viruses complexed with human monoclonal antibodies 2D22 and C10. They also performed biolayer interferometry to assess antibody binding kinetics at different temperatures.
analysis.main_results: The N153Q mutant showed increased antibody occupancy, indicating higher epitope accessibility. At 30 °C, antibodies bound more slowly to the mutant, but at 37 °C, their affinities for both wild-type and mutant viruses increased significantly.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the N153Q mutation enhances antibody recognition, which could be beneficial for vaccine development. This is a novel observation regarding the impact of glycosylation on antibody binding dynamics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into how glycosylation modifications can influence antibody neutralization, which may inform the design of more effective dengue vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which limits the depth of analysis. However, the findings are supported by structural and kinetic data, providing moderate confidence in their interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how the absence of N153 glycosylation in dengue virus 2 affects its recognition by neutralizing antibodies. Using cryoEM and biolayer interferometry, the researchers found that the N153Q mutant showed increased antibody occupancy and binding affinity at 37 °C compared to the wild-type virus. These results suggest that the mutation enhances epitope accessibility, potentially making the mutant a good vaccine candidate. The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which limits the depth of analysis but supports moderate confidence in the findings. The findings may inform the development of more effective dengue vaccines by highlighting the role of glycosylation in antibody neutralization.

title: Temporal trends in dengue incidence and mortality across surveillance case classifications: a 13-year analysis from Davao City, Philippines

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue remains a major public health concern in the Philippines, where routine surveillance systems classify reported cases as suspected, probable or confirmed. Although these classifications are widely used to monitor disease burden, their influence on the interpretation of long-term epidemiological trends and mortality patterns remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study examined the temporal trends in dengue incidence and mortality across surveillance case classifications in Davao City, Philippines, over a 13-year period. A retrospective observational study was conducted using dengue surveillance data collected from the Philippine Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (PIDSR) system from January 2012 to December 2024. A total of 81,075 dengue cases were reported during the study period, including 59,021 suspected, 20,559 probable, and 1,495 confirmed cases.
analysis.methods: Annual dengue incidence and mortality were calculated per 100,000 population, and temporal trends were assessed using the Mann–Kendall trend test. Reported dengue cases were classified as suspected, probable, or confirmed, according to the national surveillance definitions.
analysis.main_results: Confirmed dengue incidence exhibited a significant increasing trend over time ( p = 0.003), whereas probable ( p = 0.855) and suspected dengue incidences ( p = 0.059) showed no statistically significant temporal trends. Dengue mortality incidence showed no significant temporal trends in suspected ( p = 0.089), probable ( p = 0.242), or confirmed cases ( p = 0.282). Most deaths recorded among reported dengue notifications occurred among probable and suspected cases, and the highest cumulative case fatality rate was observed among probable cases (0.89%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Surveillance classifications captured distinct epidemiological patterns of dengue incidence and mortality. Increasing trends in confirmed dengue incidence were consistently observed across congressional districts, age groups, and sexes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: In low- and middle-income country (LMIC) settings, where surveillance systems operate under varying levels of diagnostic certainty, considering probable and suspected case classifications may provide additional insights into surveillance trends and mortality patterns beyond those obtained from laboratory-confirmed cases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations of the study design or evidence strength assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the temporal trends in dengue incidence and mortality across different surveillance classifications in Davao City, Philippines, over a 13-year period. It found that confirmed dengue cases showed a significant increasing trend, while probable and suspected cases did not. Dengue mortality also showed no significant trends across classifications. Most deaths occurred among probable and suspected cases, with the highest case fatality rate observed in probable cases. The study highlights the importance of considering different case classifications in understanding dengue epidemiology, especially in low- and middle-income countries where diagnostic certainty may vary. The findings suggest that surveillance data may provide additional insights into disease trends and mortality patterns beyond those obtained from laboratory-confirmed cases. The study is based on retrospective observational data and uses the Mann–Kendall trend test to assess trends.

title: Relationship between Knowledge and Attitudes in the Community with Dengue Fever Preventive Behavior in Landasan Ulin Utara Village

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the relationship between community knowledge and attitudes and dengue fever preventive behaviors in Landasan Ulin Utara Village, where dengue incidence remains high and outbreak status is ongoing.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Landasan Ulin Utara Village, involving 164 individuals aged 15–64 years, specifically heads of households or family members.
analysis.methods: Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using Spearman’s rho test to assess the correlation between knowledge and attitudes and dengue prevention behaviors.
analysis.main_results: The statistical analysis revealed no significant correlation between community knowledge and attitudes and dengue fever prevention practices in Landasan Ulin Utara Village (p = 0.193; p = 0.150).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that factors other than knowledge and attitudes may influence dengue prevention behaviors, highlighting the need to explore additional determinants such as education level, experience, and social environment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that interventions targeting knowledge and attitudes alone may not be sufficient to improve dengue prevention behaviors, emphasizing the importance of addressing broader social and environmental factors.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality, and the lack of detailed analysis on potential confounding variables, resulting in moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the relationship between community knowledge and attitudes and dengue fever preventive behaviors in Landasan Ulin Utara Village, where dengue incidence is high. A cross-sectional survey of 164 individuals aged 15–64 years was conducted using questionnaires, and Spearman’s rho test was employed to analyze the data. The results showed no significant correlation between knowledge and attitudes and prevention behaviors (p = 0.193; p = 0.150). The authors suggest that other factors, such as education level and social environment, may play a more significant role in shaping these behaviors. The findings highlight the need for a more comprehensive approach to dengue prevention, considering both individual and community-level determinants. However, the study's cross-sectional design limits its ability to establish causality, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

title: Retrospective and Contemporary Genomic Surveillance Reveals Genotype-Specific Dengue Lineage Dynamics in Rio de Janeiro

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue virus (DENV) transmission in Brazil is characterized by recurrent epidemics involving the introduction, persistence, and replacement of viral lineages. However, temporal gaps in genomic surveillance limit our understanding of how these processes shape successive epidemics in Rio de Janeiro.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, in a retrospective observational molecular epidemiology study, we combined archived genomic data with publicly available sequences and epidemiological surveillance data to investigate the temporal dynamics of DENV serotypes and lineages in Rio de Janeiro.
analysis.methods: Archived DENV-positive samples were curated and subjected to whole-genome amplicon sequencing, and the resulting consensus sequences were analyzed together with publicly available sequences using time-scaled phylogenetic reconstruction and epidemiological data.
analysis.main_results: We recovered 35 DENV genomes from samples collected in 2013, 2018, 2020, and 2021, including DENV-1 genotype V, DENV-2 genotypes II and III, and DENV-4 genotype II. Analysis of the combined datasets identified multiple Rio de Janeiro-associated clades with distinct temporal patterns.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Publicly available sequences supported the broader clade structure and long-term temporal patterns independently of most genomes generated here. The newly generated genomes made genotype-specific contributions: the five DENV-1 genotype V genomes placed archived 2020–2021 samples within previously represented Rio de Janeiro-associated groups, while the single DENV-2 genotype II genome provided phylogenetic placement of a travel-associated 2018 case.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: In contrast, the 20 DENV-2 genotype III genomes identified a Rio de Janeiro-associated cluster not represented among the public sequences, and the nine DENV-4 genotype II genomes increased representation of the 2013 epidemic.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Thus, the principal contribution of retrospective sequencing was to fill specific temporal and geographic gaps rather than to redefine the broader historical phylogenetic structure of all genotypes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the temporal dynamics of dengue virus (DENV) serotypes and lineages in Rio de Janeiro by combining archived genomic data with publicly available sequences and epidemiological surveillance. The research highlights the importance of genomic surveillance in understanding the introduction, persistence, and replacement of viral lineages during recurrent epidemics. The study recovered 35 DENV genomes, including DENV-1 genotype V, DENV-2 genotypes II and III, and DENV-4 genotype II, from samples collected between 2013 and 2021. The findings reveal distinct temporal patterns and identify a DENV-2 genotype III cluster not previously represented in public sequences. The study emphasizes the role of retrospective sequencing in filling specific gaps rather than redefining broader historical phylogenetic structures. The results contribute to the understanding of DENV lineage dynamics and have implications for surveillance and public health strategies.
